question.text: Which one of the following statements is correct?

options.text: From a mixed precipitate of $\mathrm{AgCl}$ and $\mathrm{AgI}$, ammonia solution dissolves only $\mathrm{AgCl}$.
Ferric ions give a deep green precipitate on adding potassium ferrocyanide solution.
On boiling a solution having $\mathrm{K}^{+}, \mathrm{Ca}^{2+}$ and $\mathrm{HCO}_{3}^{-}$ ions we get a precipitate of $\mathrm{K}_{2} \mathrm{Ca}\left(\mathrm{CO}_{3}\right)_{2}$
Manganese salts give a violet borax bead test in the reducing flame.

solution.text:
Ammonia can dissolve ppt. of AgCl only due to formation of complex as given below:
$$
\mathrm{AgCl}+2 \mathrm{NH}_{3} \rightarrow\left[\mathrm{Ag}\left(\mathrm{NH}_{3}\right)_{2}\right] \mathrm{Cl}
$$
